Phaser

Sweep six all-pass stages through the sound and blend them with the original.

Understand the parametersFind your starting pointWhat to listen forCommon question

Every parameter, explained

Cycle time

200 ms to 10000 ms · Default 4000 ms

The duration of the sweeping cycle. Longer values create gradual movement.

Sweep depth

0% to 100% · Default 70%

The frequency range covered by the six moving all-pass stages. Higher values make the sweep more pronounced.

Mix

0% to 100% · Default 50%

The balance of original and phase-shifted audio. The characteristic notches are strongest with both present, around 50%.

A good place to start

Try the sample or upload a short recording. Apply the defaults, compare Original and Result, then adjust one parameter at a time. Revisions on this page start from your original recording.

What to listen for

The moving phase shifts create notches when mixed with the dry signal. A 50% mix gives the clearest sweeping character.

Compare a quiet passage and a busy passage at a comfortable listening volume. The player volume changes playback only; it does not change the downloaded audio.

Can I combine this with other effects?

Yes. Open the combination studio and choose this effect along with any others. Effects run in the displayed order, and completed stages are reused. Changing or removing an earlier effect rebuilds the affected stages.

Once processing finishes, compare the result and download MP3 or WAV. MP3 encoding runs locally and does not apply the effects again.

WELCOME TO SONIC

Your sound, in three steps.

  1. Bring your audio.

    Upload a supported file, or listen to the built-in sample.

  2. Explore your effects.

    Selecting an effect includes it automatically. Adjust its settings or remove it from the chain.

  3. Listen and experiment.

    Click Apply effects, compare Original and Result, adjust and apply again, then download your WAV. Tempo preserves pitch; pitch shift preserves duration.
